name: Pekah
title: The Rebellious King of Israel
summary: Pekah was king of Israel (the Northern Kingdom) and came to power through a coup against King Pekahiah. He reigned for twenty years and is known for his alliance with Syria against Judah, as well as for losing large parts of the kingdom to Assyria. He himself was killed in a conspiracy led by Hoshea.

keyEvents.title: The Coup Against Pekahiah
keyEvents.description: Pekah, who was commander in Pekahiah's army, conspired against King Pekahiah and killed him in the royal fortress of Samaria along with fifty men from Gilead.

keyEvents.title: The Alliance with Syria
keyEvents.description: Pekah formed an alliance with Rezin, king of Syria, to attack Judah and depose King Ahaz. This threat led to the prophecy about Immanuel.

keyEvents.title: The Syro-Ephraimite War
keyEvents.description: Pekah and Rezin besieged Jerusalem but failed to capture the city. Ahaz asked Assyria for help against this alliance.

keyEvents.title: Assyrian Invasion under Tiglath-Pileser
keyEvents.description: Tiglath-Pileser III, king of Assyria, invaded Israel and conquered large areas in the north and east, taking the people into captivity in Assyria.

keyEvents.title: The Death of Pekah
keyEvents.description: Hoshea son of Elah conspired against Pekah, killed him, and became king of Israel in the twentieth year of King Ahaz of Judah.
